o: From the joined Contacts/Calls data we need the three longest calls of each type ('incoming' and 'outgoing'), with duration formatted as HH:MM:SS, ordered by type descending (so 'outgoing' rows print first), then duration descending, then first_name descending. In the example, the top-3 outgoing calls are Alice 360s, Emily 280s, Jane 240s, and top-3 incoming are Michael 420s, Jane 300s, Emily 180s. A window function numbering rows per type is the clean tool; SEC_TO_TIME handles formatting in MySQL.
k: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY type ORDER BY duration DESC) picks the top 3 per type.
SEC_TO_TIME converts seconds to HH:MM:SS; final ORDER BY type DESC, duration DESC, first_name DESC.

a.i: Join Calls to Contacts, number rows within each type by decreasing duration, keep numbers 1–3, format, and apply the required global ordering.
s: Join Calls with Contacts on contact_id = id.
Assign ROW_NUMBER() partitioned by type, ordered by duration DESC.
Filter rn ≤ 3, select SEC_TO_TIME(duration) as duration_formatted, order by type DESC, duration DESC, first_name DESC.

c.python:
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT c.first_name, cl.type, cl.duration,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY cl.type ORDER BY cl.duration DESC) AS rn
  FROM Calls cl
  JOIN Contacts c ON c.id = cl.contact_id
)
SELECT first_name, type, SEC_TO_TIME(duration) AS duration_formatted
FROM ranked
WHERE rn <= 3
ORDER BY type DESC, duration DESC, first_name DESC;

a.n: Approach 2: Per-type ordered subqueries with LIMIT
a.i: Since there are exactly two types, run one ordered subquery per type with LIMIT 3 and UNION ALL the results, applying the final sort outside. This avoids window functions entirely and is easy to reason about for a fixed small number of groups.
s: Select top 3 incoming calls (join, order by duration DESC, limit 3).
UNION ALL the two results, format durations with SEC_TO_TIME, and order by type DESC, duration DESC, first_name DESC.

c.python:
SELECT first_name, type, SEC_TO_TIME(duration) AS duration_formatted
FROM (
  (SELECT c.first_name, cl.type, cl.duration
   FROM Calls cl JOIN Contacts c ON c.id = cl.contact_id
   WHERE cl.type = 'incoming'
   ORDER BY cl.duration DESC LIMIT 3)
  UNION ALL
  (SELECT c.first_name, cl.type, cl.duration
   FROM Calls cl JOIN Contacts c ON c.id = cl.contact_id
   WHERE cl.type = 'outgoing'
   ORDER BY cl.duration DESC LIMIT 3)
) t
ORDER BY type DESC, duration DESC, first_name DESC;

w: Use the window-function version in interviews — it scales to 'top K per group' for arbitrary groups, whereas the UNION trick only works when the group set is small and known. Pitfalls: formatting seconds (SEC_TO_TIME, or LPAD-based manual HH:MM:SS in other dialects), remembering the outer ORDER BY applies after UNION, and that ties at the boundary are broken arbitrarily unless first_name is added to the window ordering. Follow-ups: top 3 per contact instead of per type, or average call duration per type.
